planner-fingerprint.sql:
select true as ok,
       'ap=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(p.updated_at) from public.assignment_progress p) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',rp=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(q.updated_at) from public.reading_progress q) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',n=' || (select count(*) from public.assignments a)::text
       || ',at=' || to_char(now() at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') as fingerprint,
       r.id as newest_request_id, r.kind as newest_request_kind, r.state as newest_request_state,
       r.created_at as newest_request_created_at, r.claimed_at as newest_request_claimed_at,
       r.finished_at as newest_request_finished_at
  from (select 1 as one) one
  left join lateral (select g.id, g.kind, g.state, g.created_at, g.claimed_at, g.finished_at
                       from public.agent_requests g
                      order by g.id desc
                      limit 1) r on true
planner-fingerprint.expect: One row, always ok: a reading, not a check. fingerprint holds the newest assignment_progress and reading_progress change, the count of assignments and the time of this read, as one string; the other columns are the newest agent_requests row.

planner-unchanged.sql:
with given as (
  select substring($1::text from '^(.*),at=') as planner,
         substring($1::text from ',at=(.*)$')::timestamptz as since
), seen as (
  select 'ap=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(p.updated_at) from public.assignment_progress p) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',rp=' || coalesce(to_char((select max(q.updated_at) from public.reading_progress q) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"'), 'none')
       || ',n=' || (select count(*) from public.assignments a)::text as planner
), moved as (
  select count(*)::integer as n, min(g.id) as first_id, max(g.id) as last_id
    from public.agent_requests g, given
   where g.created_at >= given.since or g.claimed_at >= given.since or g.finished_at >= given.since
)
select (seen.planner = given.planner) as ok,
       (moved.n > 0) as blocked,
       given.planner as planner_before, seen.planner as planner_now,
       given.since as since, now() as read_at,
       moved.n as requests_in_window, moved.first_id as first_request_id, moved.last_id as last_request_id
  from given, seen, moved
planner-unchanged.expect: One row. ok when the three planner values read the same as in the fingerprint. blocked when an agent_requests row was created, claimed or finished since the fingerprint was read: a sync or an Inbox apply ran in between, so the comparison proves nothing and the run is repeated.

turn.sql:
select (r.state = 'done' and r.error_code is null
        and m.id is not null and m.tier = $2::text and m.provider = 'claude-cli'
        and m.finished and m.error_code is null
        and ($4::text is null or $3::text is not null)
        and ($3::text is null
             or m.tool_calls @> jsonb_build_array(
                  jsonb_strip_nulls(jsonb_build_object('tool', $3::text, 'scope', $4::text, 'ok', true))))) as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.conversation_id,
       r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.finished_at,
       m.id as message_id, m.tier, m.provider, m.model, m.finished, m.error_code as message_error_code,
       (select coalesce(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object('tool', e.value->>'tool', 'scope', e.value->>'scope', 'ok', e.value->'ok')
                                  order by e.ordinality), '[]'::jsonb)
          from jsonb_array_elements(m.tool_calls) with ordinality e) as tools
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages m on m.request_id = r.id and m.role = 'assistant'
 where r.id = $1::bigint
turn.expect: One row. ok when the request is done with no error code and its answer was written at the given tier by provider claude-cli, is finished with no error code, and (when a tool is given) its tool calls hold that tool, with that scope when one is given, marked ok.

turn-stopped.sql:
select (r.state = 'cancelled' and r.error_code = 'cancelled'
        and (m.id is null or (m.finished and m.error_code = 'cancelled'))) as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.conversation_id,
       r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.finished_at,
       m.id as message_id, m.tier, m.finished, m.error_code as message_error_code
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages m on m.request_id = r.id and m.role = 'assistant'
 where r.id = $1::bigint
turn-stopped.expect: One row. ok when the request is cancelled with the code cancelled, and its answer, if the runner had begun one, is finished with the code cancelled.

turn-answered-after.sql:
select (r.state = 'done' and r.error_code is null and r.claimed_at > $2::timestamptz
        and m.id is not null and m.finished and m.error_code is null) as ok,
       r.id as request_id, r.state as request_state, r.error_code as request_error_code, r.conversation_id,
       r.created_at, r.claimed_at, r.finished_at,
       $2::timestamptz as claimed_after,
       m.id as message_id, m.tier, m.finished, m.error_code as message_error_code
  from public.workspace_requests r
  left join public.workspace_messages m on m.request_id = r.id and m.role = 'assistant'
 where r.id = $1::bigint
turn-answered-after.expect: One row. ok when the request is done with no error code, was claimed after the given time, and its answer is finished with no error code: a question that waited while the service was stopped was answered once it came back.

spike-archived.sql:
select (count(*) filter (where c.archived) = 1 and count(*) filter (where not c.archived) = 0) as ok,
       (count(*) filter (where c.archived))::integer as archived,
       (count(*) filter (where not c.archived))::integer as listed
  from public.workspace_conversations c
 where c.title = 'spike'
spike-archived.expect: One row. ok when exactly one conversation titled 'spike' is archived and none is still listed.

conversations-archived.sql:
with wanted as (
  select unnest($1::uuid[]) as id
)
select (count(*) > 0 and count(*) = count(c.id) and count(*) = count(*) filter (where c.archived)) as ok,
       count(*)::integer as asked_for,
       count(c.id)::integer as found,
       (count(*) filter (where c.archived))::integer as archived,
       coalesce(array_agg(w.id) filter (where c.id is null or not c.archived), '{}') as not_archived
  from wanted w
  left join public.workspace_conversations c on c.id = w.id
conversations-archived.expect: One row. ok when every conversation named exists and is archived; not_archived lists the ids that are missing or still listed.
